Sāyaṇa's own words carry every element: ye tvatprasādarahitā janāḥ (without Indra's grace, the hymn being addressed he indra), kepayaḥ glossed pāpakarmāṇo janāḥ (evildoers), īrmaiva as ṛṇenaiva and nyaviśanta as nīcair aviśanta, adhogatiṃ prāptāḥ (brought low by debt). Yāska as Sāyaṇa quotes him (ṛṇenaiva te nyaviśantāsminn eva loka iti vā) and as Sarup translates him ('remained here, i.e. in this very place, or in debt, or in this world') carries 'stayed in this very world, or in debt'; locator 5.25 matches Sāyaṇa's own citation (nir. 5, 25) and Sarup's section close. The difference is real though slight (Sāyaṇa narrows to debt and adds grace, evildoing and the downward course; Yāska keeps this world as an alternative) and is named, not resolved, with no ranking. Plain clause checked against day.js: v. 5 bids Indra sit on the holy grass, v. 7 wishes the evil-hearted others far away; it is context, not a paraphrase, and no four-word run from the key. Considered and not landed: 'two fates side by side' is gentler than 'sink down', but the key is printed above and rule 2 forbids restating it; Sāyaṇa cites Yāska with tathā ca, yet Yāska's extra 'this world' option is a genuine divergence. verse.js ok (ref 10.44.6, at [880,6]); entry-check ok, no errors or warns; 56 words (cap 60), one semicolon, src 141 characters.
